purpose: Source registry for the NeuraSight evidence layer. Every clinical statement in knowledge/**/*.md carries one or more of these source IDs so the generated report can cite its evidence.

verification_status.urls_verified_note: All URLs below were confirmed to exist and to be topically correct via web search on 2026-09-29.
verification_status.content_extracted_note: Full page text was NOT programmatically extracted (cancer.gov/ninds.nih.gov blocked automated fetching; NCBI Bookshelf pages did not yield text to the fetcher). The knowledge-base entries therefore state well-established, general clinical fundamentals and point to these sources for verification. They are NOT verbatim extracts and MUST be reviewed against the primary source by a qualified reviewer before any clinical framing is relied upon.

neurasight-system.title: NeuraSight system behaviour and measured evaluation results
neurasight-system.relevant_note: Used to mark statements that describe THIS SYSTEM's own scope, behaviour or measured metrics rather than making an external clinical claim. Distinguishing these from medical citations keeps the evidence audit meaningful: a sentence about what the model can and cannot do should not be dressed up with a medical reference.

nci-pituitary-pdq.title: Pituitary Tumors Treatment (PDQ)
nci-pituitary-pdq.relevant_note: Identifies inappropriate pituitary hormone secretion and visual field deficits as the most characteristic presenting features of pituitary adenomas.

nci-pituitary-diagnosis.title: Pituitary Tumors - Diagnosis and Prognosis
nci-pituitary-diagnosis.relevant_note: Describes visual field testing covering central and peripheral vision, each eye tested separately.

ncbi-pituitary-adenoma-statpearls.title: Pituitary Adenoma (StatPearls)
ncbi-pituitary-adenoma-statpearls.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 - check terms before redistribution.
ncbi-pituitary-adenoma-statpearls.relevant_note: States that diagnosis relies on pituitary-protocol MRI plus comprehensive endocrine testing, with management individualised across medical therapy, transsphenoidal surgery or radiotherapy depending on tumour type and functional status.

ninds-brain-tumors.fetch_note: Returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching; URL confirmed via search result metadata.

who-cns5.title: WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th edition
who-cns5.licence: Copyrighted publication - cite, do not reproduce.
who-cns5.relevant_note: The current authority for CNS tumour typing and grading. Integrates histology with molecular markers; grading terminology changed from the 4th edition, which matters when comparing older literature.
